client_id.description: REQUIRED. OAuth 2.0 Client Identifier valid at the Authorization Server.

response_type.description:
REQUIRED. OAuth 2.0 Response Type value that determines the authorization processing flow to be used, including
what parameters are returned from the endpoints used. When using the Implicit Flow, this value is id_token token
or id_token. The meanings of both of these values are defined in OAuth 2.0 Multiple Response Type Encoding
Practices [OAuth.Responses]. No Access Token is returned when the value is id_token.
NOTE: While OAuth 2.0 also defines the token Response Type value for the Implicit Flow, OpenID Connect does not
use this Response Type, since no ID Token would be returned.

response_mode.description:
RECOMMENDED. Response Mode is a Authorization request parameter that informs the authorization server of the
mechanism to be used for returning authorization response parameters. It's recommended to use "form_post" over
"fragment" to avoid  exposing tokens to browser history attacks, redirect headers etc.

scope.description:
REQUIRED. OpenID Connect requests MUST contain the openid scope value. If the openid scope value is not present, the
behavior is entirely unspecified. Other scope values MAY be present. Scope values used that are not understood by
an implementation SHOULD be ignored.

redirect_uri.description:
REQUIRED. Redirection URI to which the response will be sent. This URI MUST exactly match one of the Redirection
URI values for the Client pre-registered at the OpenID Provider, with the matching performed as described in
Section 6.2.1 of [RFC3986] (Simple String Comparison). When using this flow, the Redirection URI MUST NOT use the
http scheme unless the Client is a native application, in which case it MAY use the http: scheme with localhost
as the hostname.

nonce.description:
REQUIRED. String value used to associate a Client session with an ID Token, and to mitigate replay attacks. The
value is passed through unmodified from the Authentication Request to the ID Token. Sufficient entropy MUST be
present in the nonce values used to prevent attackers from guessing values.

state.description:
RECOMMENDED. Opaque value used to maintain state between the request and the callback. Typically, Cross-Site
Request Forgery (CSRF, XSRF) mitigation is done by cryptographically binding the value of this parameter with a
browser cookie.

code_challenge.description: Code challenge for Authorization Code Flow with PKCE.

code_challenge_method.description:
OPTIONAL, allowed code verifier transformation method is "S256" or "plain".
Since we support S256, we will never use plain.
